## Abstract

This work applies the GARCH-NN framework of Zhao et al. (2024) to the daily volatility forecasting of Bitcoin (BTC/USD) on a dataset of 2,375 daily observations spanning January 2017 to February 2026.

The proposed model, referred to as GARCH-LSTM, integrates a differentiable GJR-GARCH(1,1) kernel as the output gate of an LSTM cell, trained end-to-end with six blockchain on-chain metrics as exogenous features. Model parameters are optimised via Optuna with a TPE sampler (25 trials) on an NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB GPU.

The forecasting target is the 5-day realised variance proxy, a backward-looking rolling average of squared log-returns that smooths microstructure noise while preserving strict causal ordering. At each step t, the target is computed exclusively from past residuals, ensuring zero look-ahead.

$$
RV^5_t = \frac{1}{5} \sum_{k=0}^{4} \varepsilon^2_{t-k}
$$

On this smoothed target, the GARCH-LSTM achieves the following out-of-sample improvements relative to the standalone GJR-GARCH: MAE reduced by 28.1%, RMSE reduced by 17.6%, and R² improved by +0.33 points.

The optimal validation T-NLL is 2.5867, obtained at trial #17 with hyperparameters H = 32, w = 0.084, ν = 7.0, and learning rate 2.01 × 10⁻³.
